messages.subject: methRead() multiple cores
parts:
Hi MethylKit team!

I am using the function methRead() with a list of file (location = fileList). As far as I understand, methRead output three files per sample (sample1.txt, sample1.txt.bgz and sample1.txt.bgz.tbi). And it does so one by one, one sample after another. I was wondering if there is a way to parallelize the function over the number of sample. I did not find any argument like « mc.cores » (similar to calculateDiffMeth() function).

Thank you and have a nice day!

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: methRead() multiple cores
parts:
Hi Hélène,

As Ryan pointed out, parLapply can be used for this, but you should be aware that this increases the amount of available memory required. 

The way I usually do this is via mclapply (also from the parallel package). This works only on Linux and Mac, for Windows you may have to use parLapply. 

Please check out this example code: 

```
library("methylKit")
library(parallel)

file.list=list(
  system.file("extdata", "test1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
  system.file("extdata", "test2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
  system.file("extdata", "control1.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit"),
  system.file("extdata", "control2.myCpG.txt", package = "methylKit")
)

sample.ids=list("test1","test2","ctrl1","ctrl2")

treatment = c(1,1, 0,0)

res = methylRawList(
  treatment = treatment,
  mcmapply(
    FUN = methRead,
    file.list,
    sample.ids,
    assembly = "hg18",
    SIMPLIFY = FALSE,
    mc.cores = 3
  )
)  

resDB = methylRawListDB(
  treatment = treatment,
  mcmapply(
    FUN = methRead,
    file.list,
    sample.ids,
    assembly = "hg18",
    dbtype = "tabix",
    SIMPLIFY = FALSE,
    mc.cores = 3
  )
)  
```

Best,
Alex
